title: A Friday chore packaged as a skill, with its past mistakes built in
before: Mistakes I've made before: including a refactor because the title sounded exciting; calling something "Fixed" when it was really a new behavior; forgetting the platform tag.
after:
Judge by what changed, not by how exciting the title sounds. A refactor titled "New sync engine" is still a refactor. This exact mistake has happened before.
…
"Fixed" is only correct when the old behavior was a bug. If the PR adds new behavior or changes intended behavior, it belongs in New or Improved even when its title says `fix:`. Read the body and diff summary when you're unsure.
…
## 5. Verify before reporting

Check the saved file against this list and fix anything that fails:

- [ ] Every item traces back to a PR that survived the filter, and no internal, chore, refactor, or test PR made it in.
- [ ] No customer names, engineer names or GitHub handles, internal ticket IDs (such as `ABC-123` or `#123`), PR numbers, or branch names appear. Merge-commit text like "from alice/branch" is a common way these leak.
